howto_md:
## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of the whole world of music. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters. Every entry has an ID (such as MUS-01.2) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches (traditions, genres, building blocks, history, awards...).
- **Sections (MUS-01, MUS-02...)** are the main topics; each opens with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have heard or explored it.
- **Music Registers** list landmark recordings and works.
- **Tags** (#carnatic, #jazz, #yaman) and **See also** links connect related pages; instruments link to the INS index.
- Start with **Part 0**, eight two-minute questions about why music moves us.
howto_intro: This booklet is a map of the whole world of music: the classical systems of India and the world, folk and devotional songs, film music, every popular genre, the building blocks of sound, raga and rhythm, history, people, awards and ideas. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters.
Every entry has an ID (such as MUS-01.2 for Carnatic music). The same ID is the entry's address on curioussparoows.com, where each one is growing into its own page.
howto_boxes: **Parts:** the intro questions, music of the world, genres, the building blocks, history, people, awards, craft and industry, ideas, reviews, community, navigation and sources.
**Sections (MUS-01 to MUS-28):** the main topics, each opening with a *Before you start* box.
**Sub-sections and entries (☐):** one or two lines each; tick the box when you have heard or explored it.
**Music Registers:** tables of landmark recordings and honours. They are a sourced selection; the full lists grow on the website.
**Step 1.** Read Part 0, eight two-minute questions about music.
**Step 2.** Find your own region's music in Part 1, then travel to another continent.
**Step 3.** Learn the building blocks in Part 3 (swara, raga, tala, harmony).
**Step 4.** Follow tags and See also links; every instrument links to the Instruments index.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you listen, and use the tracker at the end.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 12, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
